latest_wiki.summary: Personnel of the 707th Infantry Division conducted public hangings of resistance members in Minsk, including 17-year-old Jewish nurse Masha Bruskina.
The 707th Infantry Division and attached Order Police units murdered over 10,000 individuals in Belorussia between October and November 1941, most of whom were Jews.

The text reports that Dutch police arrested four suspects in March and July 2026 over an alleged explosive or arson plot against a synagogue in Heemstede; two suspects were arrested near the synagogue with concealed fireworks in March.
A 75-year-old Jewish woman was hit and pushed to the ground because of her Jewish-sounding surname.
During the Gaza War in July 2014, death threats were expressed against Jews in Denmark.
The text reports that the Maribor Synagogue was vandalized again with threatening graffiti.
The text reports the Kielce pogrom in 1946, in which citizens violently attacked Jews after a false accusation of kidnapping a Christian child.
The text reports that the Topoľčany pogrom took place in September 1945.

During the 2012 local elections in Schaarbeek, candidates from the Jewish community were attacked for their affiliation, according to the president of the Coordination Committee of Jewish Organizations in Belgium.
The text reports the Beilis affair in Kiev, in which a local Jew was accused of killing a Christian boy and was later found innocent.

The text reports that approximately 10 attacks in March and April 2026 targeted the Jewish community in London, involving arson, explosive devices and chemicals, and hitting Jewish schools, synagogues and charities. Responsibility was claimed by Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia.
Demonstrators at an anti-Israel rally in Antwerp chanted 'Hamas, Hamas, all Jews to the gas.'

latest_jta.summary: The article reports a drive by an anti-fascist committee to remove John Smith, manager of the Brighton Beach Woolworth store, over alleged anti-Semitic statements he made.
The article reports that Nazi authorities announced that the German Jewish writers Arnold Zweig and Alfred Schirokauer would be arrested if they set foot in Germany.
The article reports that in the last few days many windows in Jewish shops in Warsaw were smashed during frequent attacks on Jews in the city's streets.
The article reports that the Protocols of the Elders of Zion are being reproduced again in Berlin, with hundreds of thousands of copies being distributed to incite hatred of Jews.
The article reports that new Ministry of the Interior regulations made it almost impossible for Jews to change their Jewish names to Nordic-sounding ones.
The article reports that the Nazi Minister of Finance announced a flight tax to be levied on Jews emigrating from the Reich.
The article refers to the latest anti-Jewish outrage in Manchuria, which it says was engineered by Russian Fascists and Prussian Nazis. The article does not describe the act.
The article reports that Jews were attacked in the center of Warsaw during a demonstration organized by the Endek National Democrats. Police arrested seventeen Endek participants.

The article reports that a district court sentenced an Endek youth to eighteen months in jail for a brutal attack on David Altman, Jewish editor of the government newspaper Glos Czestochowski. The date of the attack is not given.

The article reports that a student mob attacked the store of Zitrin, a Jewish gold trader on Rio's principal street, over a painting displayed in his window. Police arrested Zitrin to save him from the mob.

The article reports that no Jew was selected for the Paterson Grand Jury, the first such omission in many years, and that few Jews were on other juries. Local Jewish leaders linked this to an anti-Semitic atmosphere.
The article reports that the Nazi Ministry of the Interior's racial department is checking the names of all Jews and people of Jewish descent in Germany, using files of about 3,000,000 names.
The article reports that the German war blind association was told by the Nazi government that its customary subsidy would be withdrawn if blind Jewish soldiers were allowed to keep membership.

The article reports that police arrested a dismissed Jewish lawyer for displaying a 'former lawyer' sign, confiscated his stationery and brought him before a court, which fined him fifty marks. The High Court later rescinded the fine.

latest_research.summary: The Observatory on Antisemitism in Belgium reports that a paving stone was thrown through a third-floor window of the Orthodox Jewish community synagogue in Anderlecht, shattering the glass. The Observatory describes it as vandalism targeting a Jewish place of worship, and the US ambassador calls it an antisemitic attack. The perpetrator is unidentified.

Jewish News reports that a woman was filmed describing Jewish people as "killers and psychopaths" during a protest outside Sheffield Town Hall. South Yorkshire Police first recorded a hate incident. A later Jewish News report says police concluded the remarks did not amount to a recordable crime, and the lower, no-crime finding is the one noted here.

Two unknown persons threw Molotov cocktails at the Kahal Adass Jisroel synagogue complex on Brunnenstraße in Berlin-Mitte in the early morning. According to reports the devices landed on the pavement and no one was hurt.

A 26-year-old Jewish student wearing a kippah was struck on the head with a folding spade outside the Hohe Weide synagogue, according to the sources. Police assumed an antisemitic motive, and a later court ruling is reported to have found a targeted attack on a Jew.

Unknown persons scratched swastikas into several gravestones at the Jewish cemetery on Krankenhausstraße in Cloppenburg, and state security police investigated for incitement to hatred. Police later reported that two teenagers admitted the act.
Witnesses told police that a group of about 15 people gathered in front of the synagogue, shouted and burned an Israeli flag. State security police took over the investigation.

Police reported that a 24-year-old Jewish man was assaulted on a tram in Erfurt after another man noticed his Star of David necklace. The attacker tried to drag him off the tram, kicked him and later threatened him, and is being investigated for a politically motivated hate crime.

Berlin police reported that an unidentified man punched a 60-year-old man to the ground in a park after learning that he was Jewish, and the victim had minor facial injuries. State security police are investigating suspected aggravated assault with an antisemitic motive.
Unknown persons damaged the glass of the synagogue entrance door with stones, and police found a partly burned Israeli flag in front of it, according to the reports. Three suspects were arrested.

About 180 people moved from the station forecourt toward the synagogue in an unregistered rally, and antisemitic chants were shouted, according to a press report. Church bodies described the events near the synagogue as antisemitic riots.

RIAS reports that a resident of an asylum shelter in Coburg attacked another resident with a knife because he took him for a Jew. The Coburg prosecutor's office is reported to have assumed the perpetrator was not criminally responsible.

The entrance door of a residential house in Berlin-Prenzlauer Berg was sprayed with a Star of David. State security police investigated on suspicion of incitement to hatred (Volksverhetzung), and the press reported that the marking apparently aimed to intimidate Jewish residents.
